narrative:
The model has predicted a 40% chance that you will fail your final year, which means there is a significant likelihood that you may not meet the necessary requirements to graduate. As a result, you are required to take remedial courses to help improve your understanding and performance in your studies.

The prediction is influenced by several key factors. First, your mother's education level is at the primary level, which is less common among students who successfully pass their final year. This suggests that you may not have had the same level of academic support at home as many of your peers. Additionally, your father's education is also at the primary level, further indicating a potential lack of educational resources and guidance.

On a more positive note, you have not had any past failures, which typically supports a stronger chance of passing. However, the model indicates that your family relationships are rated as very poor, which can negatively impact your emotional well-being and academic motivation. Furthermore, your current health status is categorized as bad, which can affect your ability to focus and perform well in school.

Given these insights, it is crucial for you to engage in the remedial courses. These courses will provide you with the additional support you need to strengthen your understanding of the material and improve your chances of success. It may also be beneficial to seek additional support from teachers or peers, and to focus on improving your health and family relationships, as these factors can significantly influence your academic performance.
